blocks.heading: Transport methods
blocks.text: Road transport can offer flexible routes and door-to-door delivery but faces distance, road conditions and vehicle costs. Rail can suit large heavy loads on accessible routes but may require transfer at each end. Sea transport can suit bulky international cargo but takes time and requires port access. Air can suit urgent high-value light goods but is expensive for bulky low-value loads. Match speed, reliability, distance, bulk, perishability, access and cost. These are movement choices rather than definitions of wholesale or retail channels.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Nela Parts must send a small urgent high-value component, while Omi Materials moves a large non-urgent heavy load. Air may be worth considering for the urgent component if accessible and affordable; rail or sea may suit the heavy load where routes fit. Local final delivery may still require road transport.
